top_categories.workout_context: 53ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Eilat's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before December.
At mile 60 of 87, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Eilat. Train it until it feels boring.
At Gran Fondo Eilat, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Eilat. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 87 miles.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 87 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,570ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Eilat. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.weather: December in Eilat, Negev Desert, Israel. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Eilat. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Eilat’s 87 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 87 miles of mixed terrain in Eilat, Negev Desert, Israel.
